newsitem.title: ITALY: Aeroporti di Roma sees 1996 net profits jump.
newsitem.headline: Aeroporti di Roma sees 1996 net profits jump.

text.p: Aeroporti di Roma, which is controlled by Italian state holding company IRI, reported on Wednesday that its 1996 net profits rose 61 percent to 90.28 billion lire from 56.08 billion in 1995.
The group which manages the Italian capital's Fiumicino and Ciampino airports, said passenger numbers in 1996 rose 8.9 percent to 23.85 million after 21.90 million in 1995.
Group turnover rose 11.3 percent in 1996 to 1.16 trillion lire from 1.04 trillion in 1995.

The group said in a statement that it had seen considerable increases in passenger traffic to and from international destinations such as New York, Paris and London, and also between national destinations such as Milan, Palermo, Cagliari and Turin.

The statement said the board of directors was to call a shareholders meeting to approve proposals for the group to move towards a listing on the Italian bourse. Previously, the group had said it planned an initial flotation for this year and full privatisation by the end of 1998.
